utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Mr. Court Deputy, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, this is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest during the weekend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. It was slightly boring, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course. Are you ready to proceed? We'll send you home today, I hope.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hopefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We left off on Friday when we were discussing the topic of the civil protection and the public utilities company in Bratunac. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, as I understand, Mr. Mirkovic was the director of the public utilities company. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the director of the public utilities company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that was the same company that was involved in sanitation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes. It was part of that. The public utilities company was for cleaning the town, for repairing the water pipes and for the asanacija, the sanitation of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the asanacija, we said, was done by -- that was a function that was carried out by the civil protection. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And according to Mr. Mirkovic when he gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecution, the public utilities companies were established by the municipalities. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was probably the case that these companies were established by the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that it was the Municipal Assembly, according to Mr. Mirkovic, that appointed the director. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Mirkovic also stated to the Office of the Prosecution when he gave a statement that Mr. Simic, who was president of the Municipal Assembly, Mr. Davidovic, who was president of the executive board, and Mr. Deronjic who was the President of the SDS party in Bratunac were the ones who would submit or order the restoration of the terrain or asanacija.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm going to object to this line of questioning. I know Mr. Karnavas has asked a number of questions relating to Mr. Mirkovic's statement. He's simply reciting a statement of a witness who is not here. It's not testimony. In my respectful submission, it's objectionable. He cannot simply recite another witness's statement in this fashion. He's essentially testifying on behalf of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that Defence counsel could ask any questions which might go to the credibility of this witness or may go to the point raised by the Prosecution in the direct. As for the reading of the statement -- Mr. Karnavas, I think you have to ask a direct question to this witness. If you did not get the answer you want, you may put your case before this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I wasn't reading by the way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But not the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. I understand. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As I have indicated, according to your komandir who was a director of the public utilities and was also the komandir of the civil protection, he indicated that the president of the Municipal Assembly, the president of the executive board, and the president of the SDA party were the ones that would order him to do sanitation. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Karnavas has just asked the same question he asked previously which I objected to and as I understood your ruling he wasn't permitted to put the form of the question in that manner. I'm not sure I understand why Mr. Karnavas is continuing to ask the same question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has contended that this gentleman and his supervisor were working under the military and not the civil government. The objection that was raised, there was an assumption that I was reading from the statement. I have not read from the statement. I've indicated that his supervisor, his komandir has indicated that it was the municipal authorities that were giving the orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's go step by step. First off, you lay some foundations for your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe I did do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think so. You directly asked the witness what somebody said. Lay some foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, okay. Very well, Your Honour. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could go back to some of the topics that we covered on Friday. Mr. Mirkovic was your komandir when he was the head of the civil protection. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it was the civil protection that was engaged in the task of asanacija. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the civil protection relied on the use of the public utilities company in carrying out those functions during that period. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that Mr. Mirkovic, your komandir, would be in a pretty good responsible to know who would be responsible for giving the orders to him for asanacija. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was supposed to know; I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the Prosecution on Friday was trying to assert that the task of asanacija was under the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey can object. He doesn't need to whisper to his co-counsel, your honour. I have no problems with either one of them objecting. I really don't

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we will acknowledge the formal objections, but not whispers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, was it your understanding that the civil protection was under the military or was it part of the civilian authority?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not familiar with the chain of command, however, the civil protection was only involved with the asanacija of the terrain and, as I've already said, repairing the water and telephone lines. As for any further structure of the government, I was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've indicated that you got your orders during those days from Mr. Nikolic in the presence of your komandir, Mr. Mirkovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mirkovic has indicated in his statement to the Office of the Prosecution that he was personally ordered by Colonel Beara. Do you know who Colonel Beara is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I'm not familiar with those officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So I take it that at no time during this period did you ever receive an order from someone named Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, I want to talk to you a little bit about your interview in Banja Luka. You were interviewed back on June 29th, 2002. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it you had to go from Bratunac to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you drive or did you take a bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drove in my own car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And is that a six- to eight-hour drive? Is that what it took you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It takes at least six hours if you go through the Federation. If you take the long way around, it takes at least eight to nine hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And which way did you go through?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went across the Federation by Tuzla and Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it you got there the night before the interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I set out at 2.00 in the morning and I arrived in Banja Luka at 7.30 or 8.00 the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the interview began around 9.00, did it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the morning, around 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And according to the transcript, it ended slightly after 5.00 p.m., some eight hours later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at half past 4.00 or 5.00, the breaks were long, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now -- and during the interview, you were interviewed by two people, plus there was an interpreter in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe one was a man and the other one was a woman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the man, Mr. Piekos, who was the investigator, did most of the questioning, did he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the man was the one asking most of the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But occasionally the female, Ms. de la Torre, would interrupt and ask questions as well. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She asked some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at times she would interrupt you and ask you to be more direct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was something she couldn't understand, but that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, as the interview began, you were told that your status -- you had the status of a suspect. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what they said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And they told you that depending on what they learned from you, that perhaps your status might change further down the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's precisely what they told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Would it be fair to say that made you somewhat apprehensive and nervous?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a very unpleasant experience, yes. I didn't trust them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But nonetheless you tried to answer their questions, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to answer all the questions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, on Friday, the Prosecutor pointed out a segment in your statement where you seemed to indicate that the -- when you were doing this work as part of the asanacija, that you were under the Bratunac Brigade and under the command of Vidoje Blagojevic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She asked me a question and I provided an answer. Now what the answer was, I can't remember. Probably the public utilities company was under the command of the Bratunac Brigade throughout that period of time. I think that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But then when I questioned you, you indicated that it was part of the civilian authority and not under the military. Do you remember when I questioned you on Friday, you then indicated that it was your understanding that the civil protection is under the civil authority and not under the military authority?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said, however, as for that period of time when all this was happening, whether it was under civilian or military command, I really don't know. But that was indeed what my answer was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. That's your answer today as well, you're unsure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The structure of the chain of command while all this was happening -- I'm not precisely familiar with it, but that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, Colonel Blagojevic was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that he was the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He never gave you an order, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He never asked you to do any asanacija, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when Mr. Nikolic came to you in front of Mr. Mirkovic and ordered you, Mr. Nikolic never said that he had an order from the commander of the Bratunac Brigade for you to carry out, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He never said that to us. What he did say was for us to do it, but he never said who had ordered him to carry this out. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course you knew Mr. Nikolic from before when, as I understand it, you had indicated he was the commander of the brigade or the Territorial Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. Before all these events, he was in the military department and for a while he was a teacher, that sort of thing. That's what I knew him from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But you indicated to the Prosecution that he had been the first commander when the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But if it was in the transcript of your statement, you would have no reason to doubt that you had stated that? If it was in your transcript that you gave, you would have no reason to doubt that, would you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what I said, I would have no reason to doubt that. But frankly, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just for the record let me read what you said in from your statement and I'm reading from the updated, revised, corrected version of your transcript given to us by the Office of the Prosecution. It's on page 37, line 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And incidentally, Your Honours, I don't believe there was a Prosecution number given to this particular exhibit. So I believe that we may need to give it a number. And since we're introducing it, it should come under D66/1 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, can I interrupt you, please, it will be D67/1 ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you for correcting me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You indicate: "At the beginning of the war, the brigade commander was Momir Nikolic." And then on page 38 -- in the B/C/S version, it would be on page 22 sort of in the middle of the page. And I'll wait for you to get it. You were asked a question, this is on page -- I'm reading from page 37, line 16. In your version it would be page 22, and it's around line 8. "Do you know the members of the command of the Bratunac Brigade?" Answer: "At the beginning of the war, the brigade commander was Momir Nikolic." And then on page 38, further down in your text you say: "At the beginning of the war he was the one who commanded the brigade and during the time when the operation of Srebrenica, I think it was Blagojevic, Vidoje." So I take it that you knew Mr. Nikolic to be someone of authority in Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I assumed, but that's precisely what I said, that he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Exactly. Now, since we're talking about Mr. Nikolic, as I understand it, at some point after the burials and prior to the reburials, you began receiving anonymous phone calls, your family, you and your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And those phone calls were threats of what would happen to you and your children. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you took those threats quite seriously, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took them seriously, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then after the threats came Momir Nikolic to visit you? After the anonymous phone calls, at some point Momir Nikolic came to visit you to direct you to do the reburials?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, not at home. But as I understand it, the sequencing of it was there anonymous phone calls and then at some point Momir Nikolic again gave you an order that you had to do the reburial.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was outside the wooden shack where the police were. That's where he wanted us to come. That's where he called us, not at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And I'm not suggesting that he was calling you at home. But I want to make sure that we all understand that first you got the anonymous phone calls threatening your family if you did not participate in the activities they wanted you to participate in. And then after that, at some point it was Momir Nikolic who came and ordered you to carry out the activities for which you and your family had been threatened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were ordered to do the reburial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it the anonymous phone calls stopped once you agreed to carry out the orders given to you by Mr. Nikolic? You didn't receive any threatening calls, any anonymous calls after you agreed to carry out the orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no further calls, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, if I could return.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we would like to clarify two dilemmas concerning Friday's testimony by this witness and today's testimony by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] (redacted).

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we shall keep this very brief. Can we have the usher's assistance, please? (redacted). (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could I just ask to have his statement put before him, the one that was exhibited a few moments ago. Mr. Witness, could you just look at the B/C/S version of your statement on page 3. I'm going to read out part of your statement, that particular part, so then let's comment upon it together. In response to the question put by the investigator: "We are looking for the main perpetrators which does not preclude the possibility of --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down, the interpreters do not have the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: "-- the main perpetrators, but this does not mean that those who are of minor importance are of interest as well." Answer: "What I did with the machine that's a different story, but I was an ordinary grave digger, if I can put it that way." Have you found this section?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the English original version, it is page 4, Your Honours. And now I would just like to ask you to look at page 13 of the B/C/S version. On page 8 of the B/C/S version, which is page 13 of the English version, the original version. You say the following: "I did not even enter Srebrenica because I went down to the asphalt road below Vidikovac and then the military Motorola asked me to come to Bratunac, because on both sides there were dead people. They were supposed to be buried in order to prevent an infection." Did you manage to read that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this particular section of your statement, I would just like to put a few questions to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You were treated by them as a suspect. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you did not know why you were a suspect in view of the work you had done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic. Take your time and we need to have the proper translation. Please make a pause after you hear the answer of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: These two answers, are they precisely the result of this fact why you did not feel guilty, you wanted to avoid an infection from breaking out and you simply had to do this job, that is to say bury the dead?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. I don't feel guilty because I was involved in a humanitarian matter in order to prevent an infection from breaking out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'll just try to clarify another question. On Friday you spoke about a machine BGH-900 and it had the lettering Vodovod Zvornik on it and it had been there for a longer period of time in order to deal with the river bed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During those days when you worked in Glogova, did you see any one of the machinists from Zvornik use this particular machine or does your knowledge pertain to the fact that you used the machine only?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody came from Zvornik. Nobody was there. I was the only one who during that period of time when I was told that this machine had to be used -- I mean, they brought it there. I worked with it on the second day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So I'm correct if I infer that you did not see anyone from Zvornik operating that machine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no one else there. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect? Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave I would just like to draw your attention to one thing. I have no special questions, I'm not going to raise anything, but I would just like to draw your attention to one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, is it a procedural matter or is the matter concerning of the substantial issues?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it has to do with P-160.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Blagojevic, I think we have already passed that witness already. Now this witness is P-140.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but I meant exhibit P-160 that was mentioned here on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. Blagojevic, you may raise a question or make a statement, but I have to warn you that anything you said may be used as evidence against you, and you voluntarily give up your right to remain silent. You have to understand that before you make any interventions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we have already advised you that if you have any questions or issues, you may write down on a piece of paper and pass it to your counsel. Are you going to still make that intervention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I still wish to intervene, Your Honour. I have already presented my position, but I don't want to repeat it every morning here in respect of whether I have a lawyer or not here. I think that this can be found in the transcript and I don't want to tire the Trial Chamber here time and again. I abide by the position I've already taken. I wish to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, so long as you understand the legal consequences, you may proceed, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everything I am doing I am doing with good intentions, I mean in respect of myself and the institution. So this is what it has to do with: As far as this particular exhibit is concerned, the Prosecution Exhibit P-160, and it has to do with -- I think it was a copy that was shown here on the ELMO, a copy of the document, a certificate that the witness brought here. I would like to state here that if we look at the institution that is mentioned in the upper left-hand corner of this document and the person who signed this document and is mentioned in the lower right-hand corner of that document, that person is not authorised to issue this kind of document, or rather, a document with this kind of substance. A document of this kind of substance or with a similar substance should have been issued by the Bratunac Brigade. And then it would be authentic. This has to do with some other matters. I could comment on that, too, but I would not wish to because from the very outset I have to say that I think this is a document that is worthless, bearing in mind the institution that the mentioned in the upper left-hand corner and also the person that signed the document on the -- in the lower right-hand corner, because this is not a person who commanded the Bratunac Brigade and this is not a person that had anything to do with the Bratunac Brigade. That is what I wish to say to you, Your Honours, and I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, in your statement when you gave your statement at Banja Luka to investigators on the 29th of June, 2002, did you tell them at that point that Dragan Mirkovic was working under the supervision of the Bratunac Brigade in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I said this, but Dragan Mirkovic was in this public utilities company.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you tell them that the public utilities company was working under the supervision of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I said that because I understood the system, but then perhaps that was not the system, of command I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you say to the investigators that perhaps that that was not the system of command at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier on that I don't know this system, but I did say that the public utilities company worked on this sanitisation and the repairs and everything. Now, whether it was within the Bratunac Brigade, perhaps I did say it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Well, just to clarify, I'm going to refer to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I would ask the usher to please hand a copy of the B/C/S version to the witness. Thank you. I'm referring, Your Honour, to the bottom of page -- starting with page 35, line 19.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in your version, sir, page 21, line 25. And you were asked the following.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Could you explain to me the chain of command over yourself. First of all, you told that your commander was Mr. Mladjenovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was in charge of the Workers' Battalion. When I was in Oblovac at the front lines this Nedjo Mladjenovic was commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Does it mean, that you changed your unit or responsibility also command upon arrival to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had to change because we were being in the Workers' Battalion, and this company that was doing the public utilities was also part of that. So when I would serve at the lines, I would serve under Nedjo and when I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no. Too fast.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I will slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: A. So when I would serve at the lines, I would serve under Nedjo and when I would go there, I would be under the command of Dragan Mirkovic who was in charge of that particular unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Mirkovic, Dragan, was your permanent commander and was under supervision of the command of Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. He was the commander, officer in the public utilities and he was the one who gave me the orders and he was receiving the orders from the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know specifically whom he was subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't take interest in that. I don't know. Somebody in the command, but I don't know who it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know the members of the command of the Bratunac Brigade? And then you begin to say:

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war it was Momir Nikolic and then it was Vidoje Blagojevic. Do you recall being asked those questions and giving those answers, sir? Do you recall being asked those questions and giving those answers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right. Those were the answers given.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Just for further clarification, I would like to refer to page 8, starting at line 10. Page 6 in the B/C/S version, starting at line 9. You were asked the following question, sir, and gave the following answers:

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What did you do at the beginning of the war? Your activities between 1992 and 1995, up to July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war, I received my draft note and I was immediately put into the engineering unit. I was working on the asanacija of the terrain, meaning --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please slow down. It is too fast.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- meaning I was mostly burying the dead from both sides of the battle, both the Serbian side of the -- Then it says indiscernible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What was the Engineering Unit, what brigade was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the only brigade from the Bratunac Brigade. That was the only engineering company in the Bratunac Brigade and it actually belongs -- it's part of the public utilities service. Do you recall, sir, giving -- being asked those questions and giving those answers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those were the questions that were put and those were the answers given, that the Bratunac public utilities company -- I mean, I belonged to this Bratunac utility company, and this was a unit that was involved in the sanitisation of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it also says that unit was part of the Bratunac Brigade at the time, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that structure I didn't know that, that's what I said. But if this structure is correct or then if it's not correct, I mean I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I could have the Court's indulgence. I just want to refer to my notes for a moment, Your Honour. Sorry, Your Honour, I just misplaced a document for a moment. Thank you for your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm going to show you a document which is marked P-160, page 5. And if I can ask the assistance of the usher to place this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And perhaps, Your Honour, we can go into closed session briefly before we do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Actually, I think it should be closed session, Your Honour, because it will be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in the open session. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time I was ordered by Dragan Mirkovic, who was my superior, to dig that pit in Glogova. Present there was also Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And when you were told to dig this ditch, what date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I gave the exact date. That was following the fall of Srebrenica, two or three days after the burial of the Serb soldiers, which would make it the third day after the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: After the fall or before the fall? You stated that you were not to dig a ditch before the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not when this was said, nor would this have been possible because I was on the line back then. That was after my arrival back in the public utilities company on the 13th or the 14th, I was told to report back to the public utilities company on the 15th to go and dig the graves in Glogova. That was after the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I don't mean to interrupt, but I just want to clarify Judge Vassylenko I believe was referring to the Redzici grave in 1992, which is the subject of the information report. It seems to me that perhaps the witness misunderstood and was referring to the graves that he's already testified about, the Glogova graves. I wanted to clarify that because I noticed that the witness perhaps did not understand the question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Your Honour. I just wanted to perhaps refer Your Honour to the very last page that reflects the comments of the investigator, deals with the -- it says it relates to a 1992 grave. I hope I've clarified matters, Your Honour. I was just trying to assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, do you have any questions out of Judge's question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, I don't. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At this stage are there any documents to tender on the side of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll be tendering the following documents under seal, P-160, that's the full package of documents that I referred to earlier. P-164, P-165, and I believe P-161 refers to the name of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But here we have a witness under the protective measures. If you want to tender P-161, I believe that before your direct examination you have to show this piece of the paper to the witness himself, to the party -- to the other party, and to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it was my mistake, Your Honour, but I was under the impression that he was shown the paper and I acknowledged that name as being himself. And perhaps I just misrecollected that. And if that's the case, we can simply do that at this point. I don't believe that would be in dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think there is any dispute. It's just the procedural matters. We'll see if there's any objections from the other side. If there's no objections, why should we --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. Do you have any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't have any objections, however, I concur with your remarks with respect to 161. It's my recollection that it was never shown, his name on the document, and I think that we should follow the established procedure, just to be on the safe side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any objections to those four documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for our Defence team, no, Your Honour. There are no objections, nor do we challenge anything related to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These four documents are admitted into evidence under seal, because all the documents bear the name of this witness. At this stage, are there any documents to tender on the Defence part? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not from us, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: When the usher pulls up the blinds, she will take you out of the courtroom and we wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, I believe that the next witness is also under the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Mr. President. He has asked for a pseudonym and face distortion. And could we go into -- well are we still in private session just by the looks of things or could we go to private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no. We could go to private session, please.
