utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Witness, on -- did you receive any kind of an assignment related to security in the Hotel Fontana around the time of the attack on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Hotel Fontana was the command post of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. So I received orders to provide security for that command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when did you receive orders to provide security for the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was when those main officers came, the officers from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. This was maybe a few days before the fall of Srebrenica. I don't remember exactly, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And who gave you the orders to secure the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That order was issued by Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you say the Hotel Fontana was a command post. Were there any -- was there any communications equipment for the command to use to communicate outside the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't enter the hotel, and at that time it was not allowed to enter the hotel. So the military police provided security in front of this facility, I mean Fontana.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So did you have any idea what was going on inside the hotel when there was superior officers there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just know that two or three meetings were held. I know that the representatives of the Muslim people came to this one meeting, then the representatives of the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you about that. The day or evening that the Muslim representatives came to that hotel with the representatives of the United Nations, were you asked or ordered, excuse me, to provide any more security for the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Orders were given then to reinforce the security of the Fontana Hotel and members of the civilian police took part in this as well, of the police station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did you yourself go to the hotel to help with security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just came once to see the place. It was not allowed to enter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where were you coming from before going to the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came from the facility where the military police headquarters were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in front of the brigade command. This is a facility that was outside the compound belonging to brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. On that day that you left the MP post and went over to the Hotel Fontana to check on security, do you know where your commander, Blagojevic, was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know where he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So where did you go after going to the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went back to the military police headquarters up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And about what time did you get back to the military police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was in the evening. I don't know. Perhaps about 2200 hours, something like that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what did you do that evening after getting back from checking on the security of the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When this security was over, when this meeting was over, the policemen who were engaged in providing security there returned to this facility, and they were on the ready. Because orders were given prohibiting anyone to leave the premises, I mean the place where the military police was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did any superior officers come back to the Bratunac Brigade command that night to your knowledge or come to it, I should say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I don't know. I didn't have the right to know whether anybody returned to the brigade command or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were your military police units assigned to providing any security for superior officers that were in the area at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which time you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The evening of the Hotel Fontana and the next day and the next day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that before that, there was security at the Fontana Hotel and afterwards, too. For as long as the command was there, or rather, members from the Main Staff -- for as long as the officers of the Main Staff were there, the military police secured the facility.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you -- were any military policemen assigned to be with General Mladic to travel with him as his security as he went around the area around Bratunac on those days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The military police provided security for his movements every day. Wherever he went, they provided security for him as well as along the route that he would take.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: How about for General Krstic, did your military -- did the Bratunac Brigade military police provide security for General Krstic during this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that they provided security for all the officers of the Main Staff and of the corps, but I know also that there was military police from the corps. It was called the battalion of the military police from the corps, and there were some of them who came there with them. And they also provided security.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who was the commander of the corps of the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what his name was. I've forgotten his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how many military policemen from the corps were there in Bratunac during these days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't know them anyway. I knew this commander of that detachment of the military police of the battalion, but I don't know. I didn't know these men, so I cannot say what their number was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you give us a rough idea, just a rough estimate. More than a hundred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You have no idea whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You have no idea whatsoever? You need to speak into the mike, remember.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm saying that I didn't know them. I mean, if I saw some soldiers there, how could I know who they belonged to and which unit they belonged to, perhaps I didn't even see them. I mean, if I would see them at one place, how can I know whether they're not in another place, too. Perhaps they're providing security for somebody else from the corps, too. How can I say? I cannot give any figure because I would be making a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you know if General Mladic came to the Bratunac Brigade command the night that the Muslims and the Dutch met at the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see him. I mean, I was not in a position to see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You said he was provided security by your people. Wouldn't your people have reported to you his movements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not authorised to check on where the General is going. So they did not have the duty to inform me about that, about his movements.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your military police officers did not have a duty to report to you about what they had been doing with General Mladic. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, what are you telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what I'm supposed to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just do your best to answer the questions and tell the truth. What else did you do that night when you got back from the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what I did. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You have no idea?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. How about the next morning, which would be the 12th July. What did you do the morning of the 12th July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember those dates. I cannot remember that time, I mean because it's been quite a while since then.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, don't worry about the dates. That's why I've made an effort to say the day after the night of the Hotel Fontana meeting with the Muslims and the UN. What did you do the next day? Were you aware of another meeting at the Hotel Fontana that morning of that next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I've already said that there were two or three meetings, perhaps even more. I don't know. I don't know what the first one was, whether the first one was with these representatives of the United Nations and of the Muslim people or whether that was the last meeting. I mean, I don't know. I can't remember the exact order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, just tell us about the morning after the evening of the first meeting. Were you on duty? This is the day that the VRS first went into Potocari, just to help refresh your recollection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that one night I was assistant duty officer for Momir Nikolic. Now, which night that was and what the date was, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll get to that, but first I want to talk about -- you're aware that the VRS went into Potocari one morning, weren't you? Were you aware that the VRS one morning went into Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What were you doing that morning that the VRS went into Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not even know that this action was being prepared. I did not even know that an action was being prepared to attack Srebrenica. When General Mladic left, I don't know which day that was, which date that was, when he went up to Srebrenica -- no, not to Srebrenica, to Potocari, to Potocari. When he went to Potocari, military police security went with him. And then he was giving something out to the Muslim people who were gathered there in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. That day that General Mladic first went to Potocari, how many of the Bratunac Brigade military police went with him as security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I know that he himself could have returned a number of military policemen. He could have said, I don't need you, something like that. So this number changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, please, just listen. It's a simple question. How many Bratunac Brigade military police went to secure General Mladic that first day he went into Potocari, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that number, I don't. Perhaps four or five, perhaps more. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you give -- excuse me. Did the military police have an assignment separate from securing General Mladic in Potocari that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It did not have a separate assignment. They accompanied him and they were providing security along the route. Which date that was, I can't remember. It was the route towards Pribicevac. So the military police secured the road to Pribicevac and they accompanied General Mladic. So there were some who directly accompanied him and others provided security along the road to Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were there any Bratunac Brigade military police securing the crowd of Muslim refugees that was in Potocari that first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were there any Bratunac Brigade military police assisting the Muslim refugees to getting on the buses and transported out of Potocari that first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you receive any reports from anyone that Bratunac Brigade military police were securing Muslim people in Potocari that day, besides ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not have that task. Their task was to accompany General Mladic to provide security for him personally, not for somebody else who happened to be there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know if military police separated Muslim men from the crowd of Muslims in Potocari that first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you order Bratunac Brigade military police to secure the crowd of Muslims in Potocari that first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The military police did not secure the Muslims on that day at all in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you give them any orders, the military police, any orders to secure Muslims in Potocari that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: How about the next day, the second day that Muslims were transported out of Potocari, were the -- did you know whether the military police were involved in securing the Muslims on that second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police did not have that task at all to take part in this transport or to separate people, board them, anything. They did not have that duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you ever hear any reports that they were involved in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So that first day that Mladic went into Potocari, did you go into Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only went to the point where the entrance was into the UN base, or the base of the Dutch Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there just to see whether the military policemen were still there, the ones who were providing security for General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what did you find?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many members of the United Nations there, of the Dutch Battalion, that is. There were a lot of troops from some units that I didn't even know who that were not from the Bratunac Brigade. I saw General Mladic at a distance of about 50 to 100 metres by a fence, which was on the left-hand side when facing Srebrenica, where there were Muslims, primarily women and children. And he was giving them something across this fence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So did you see any of your military -- did you see any military police officers from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time there were military policemen who were providing security for General Mladic personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And who were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, it looks like it's our break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will resume at 12.30. --- Break taken at 11.59 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So, Mr. Witness, when you were in Potocari and you said you were watching General Mladic, did you issue any orders at that time to anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you receive any orders from anyone at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned to the police building.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what did you do there that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Not a thing? Did you issue any orders? Receive any orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you receive any reports from any military police from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember really.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to Exhibit P-92, and if we could give the witness the 12 July -- in B/C/S it says 12, 13 July. This is the -- one of the daily -- well, we'll let you see what this is and ask you about it. Do we have the English that we could put on the ELMO for the -- it says 12, 13 of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we are in the open session. Is it safe?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you're looking at the original B/C/S version of this page. Can you tell us what this is that's dated 12, 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an operations logbook for the duty operations officer of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how is it normally filled in? Who does it and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is done by the duty officer of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is it done the same time each day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Roughly what time should it be done each day if you're doing it according to the rules or the practices that you worked by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is usually written down before another duty officer takes over. I think it was at 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So this says on this particular one, 12, 13 July. What time do you think these notes would have -- or what day do you think these notes would have been written down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These notes were written down on the 13th, because it says here 12th of July, 13th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So let's go over some of the information in here. So would this information -- it was written down at 7.00 a.m., the 13th of July. I take it this information would have been for the 12th of July then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And let's look at that first sentence. "The police were engaged in securing the UNHCR and the surrender of Muslim people from Srebrenica in Zuti Most to the Serb soldiers in Bratunac." Let me ask you about the first part of that, "The police were engaged in securing the UNHCR." Do you know what is meant by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just have a look. I don't know. This perhaps refers to the members of the international forces. I don't know. The UN or the UNHCR, maybe the International Red Cross. As for the surrender of Muslims from Srebrenica and Zuti Most, at Zuti Most there was a checkpoint manned by the military police. They were there all the time securing the checkpoint. That's where the confrontation line was between Bratunac and the Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were Muslims surrendering to them at Zuti Most? What does that reference mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The Muslims were not surrendering at Zuti Most. This probably refers to a convoy that was coming from the Potocari area into the area of Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Convoy of what? You mentioned a convoy, sir, a convoy of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A convoy with the refugees from Srebrenica. The people who were transported -- or rather, from Potocari, who had been in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Then the next sentence says: "One part of the police forces secured the sick and wounded in the clinic." First of all, who were the sick and wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sick and wounded were Muslim people, the Muslim population who had been wounded around Srebrenica and then transported to the health centre in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And then it says: "One part of the police forces secured the sick and wounded in the clinic, and the passage of trucks transporting refugees from the Srebrenica enclave through Bratunac." So what in particular, if you know, is meant by "Securing the passage of trucks transporting refugees from the Srebrenica enclave through Bratunac"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The families of civilians who had been killed and soldiers who had been killed, too, from the municipality of Bratunac were furious, furious with the Muslim people, because they would not allow them through the territory of Bratunac. They stoned the convoy. So in order to prevent that from happening, the police provided security for those vehicles to pass through safely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Why was the Serb population furious with the Muslim population at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because on several occasions there were attacks from the protected enclave of Srebrenica and the zone around Srebrenica, attacks by armed groups coming out of Srebrenica attacking villages such as Bjelovac, Kravica, and other towns in Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So how well known was it that the Serb populations were very angry with the Muslims were these attacks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just a minor clarification. He's referring to Serb population as if it's the entire Serb -- everybody who was Serb in that area. I believe the gentleman indicated that families of soldiers who had been killed as opposed to the Serb population. I just want to make sure that the record doesn't reflect that there's some kind of collective, you know, Serb outrage out there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, is that an important issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I think at some point it does become an important issue, because now we're talking about the entire Serb population being against the Muslim population. I thought this entire process was so that we get away from collective guilt and we focus on individual responsibility, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think there is any doubt about that, but anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I don't know why that allegation needs to raise its head at me. It's certainly not anything I'm trying to suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not raising an allegation. I'm just asking that he be a little more precise. That's all

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe, Mr. McCloskey, you can ask some questions of this to clarify the issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This feeling, this wartime -- I take it this is a wartime feeling that the families of those killed by the Muslims felt. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was felt by the Serb people, those in particular whose family members had been killed. Both civilian victims -- because many civilians had been killed and soldiers, Serb soldiers, that had been killed by the Muslims from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So as far as you know, did both the Muslims and the Serbs have many friends and family killed on both sides in this war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you were aware that there were some rather hard feelings felt in Bratunac town on this particular day when the Muslims were being transported through it. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. The next reference is: "Night duty in Fontana." Is that the security you've talked about earlier because of the superior officers staying there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's the security for the Fontana Hotel. And here it says "the UNHCR school." I think that's security being provided -- well, it reads UNHCR, but I think that's a mistake, probably the reference is to DutchBat, members of the Dutch Battalion who were being billeted at the secondary school building, the secondary school centre in Bratunac, that's where they were billeted, so that's where security was being provided. Breakfast and lunch at the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the evening of the 12th of July, this first day that Muslims were transported out of Potocari towards Kladanj, what was your assignment in the evening, besides what we see from that logbook? What were you personally doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What were you doing this night, this first day that Muslims were transported?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I may have been on duty that night. I know that I was the assistant duty officer at the brigade headquarters, at the operations centre, one of those nights, and this may have been the night.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was there any superior officers at the brigade command when you were assistant duty officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What time would you have begun your assistant duty officer job at the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty was 24 hours, around the clock, from 7.00 in the morning the first day until 7.00 in the morning the next day. Momir Nikolic was the duty officer and I was the assistant. So as a rule before this situation arose, as part of our regular activities, he would have been on duty for 12 hours between 7.00 in the morning and 7.00 in the evening, and then I would have taken over at 7.00 in the evening and 7.00 the next morning. However, when these activities began related to Srebrenica, and during the day he would call me if he needed me, and then I would take over and stand in for him. And then he would return, and as soon as he returned, he would tell me, "I'm taking over, you can go and get some rest now." So, I couldn't give you the exact hours when I was on duty and when Nikolic was on duty, respectively. I can't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you were in Potocari that first day and when you saw General Mladic, did you see Momir Nikolic in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you on duty as assistant duty officer in the evening hours of that first day of the transportation of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on duty. I'm not sure if it was the first or the second day, but I know that I was assistant duty officer for one day during the night and morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Where was the assistant duty officer's office in the brigade headquarters, roughly just? What floor, to begin with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty room, the duty operations room was on the ground floor of the building where the Bratunac Brigade headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how close to the entry way where people enter into the brigade headquarters was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, between 30 and 50 metres, 40 metres from there, perhaps 30.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That evening you were duty officer, what do you recall -- what information do you recall receiving regarding the whereabouts of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember any information. It was written the same way as the operations logbook. There was another duty book detailing all activities and reports received from units or officers. This was all recorded in the duty logbook.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That evening that you were duty officer, did you know where your commander, Blagojevic, was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The next day, which is the second day that people were transported out of Potocari, Muslim people, what were you doing in the morning? Were you on duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure which day you're referring to, but I know that I was on duty until 7.00 or 8.00 on that day, as long as we're talking about the 13th. I think -- I don't know. I was on duty that day but not the following day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. If we could -- I want to show you a conversation. I know you've seen it before. And we don't want to put it on the ELMO, but if you could --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, we should probably go into private session I think for this brief line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So it might be a good idea to put it on the ELMO just to assist us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you want to put it on the ELMO, we'll have to go to closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Does everybody have a copy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted). (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, you may answer the question, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what I did that day. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember in my office on Sunday telling me -- beginning an account regarding something you did that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember what I did exactly on each one of those days. Now, one day I went to Konjevic Polje. Is that the day? I mean, I don't know whether that's the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, the day that you went to Konjevic Polje, was that the same day that you went up towards Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Which day was it in relation to when you went up towards Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The day before I went to Zvornik, the day before that I went to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, tell us about that day then, the day you went to Konjevic Polje, and tell us what you first recall. Did you notice any senior officers anywhere that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for senior officers, I saw General Mladic and Colonel Popovic, Vujadin Popovic. I saw them within the compound of the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And did you want to correct a mistake you made. I think you testified to it earlier, but it was it was pretty out of context. Some people may have caught it, about when you first saw General Mladic and General Popovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean before the work concerning Srebrenica started?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No. You -- to help refresh your recollection, you've told us in Banja Luka that you saw General Mladic and Colonel Popovic the same day that you took people up to Zvornik. And you have, I believe, changed your account on that a little bit. Can you tell me about when you first saw General Mladic and General Popovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When -- I mean, I know that I took an APC. I did not remember that in Banja Luka, and I did not say that I went to Konjevic Polje, because I know that I saw then -- I mean, when I first rode in this APC, I first saw General -- Colonel Popovic and General Ratko Mladic. That's when I first saw them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you saw General Mladic and Colonel Popovic that for the first time when you took the APC to Konjevic Polje. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So where was it when you first saw General Mladic and Colonel Popovic? Where were you? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the entrance into the brigade headquarters. There's a policemen on duty there at the entrance, at the gate, leading into brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you outside the building of the headquarters or inside the building at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside the compound, outside the compound of the brigade headquarters and outside the building, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And who did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw General Mladic and Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: About what time of day was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Maybe around noon. I don't know what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And what's the first thing you remember happening when you saw these guys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic swore at Colonel Popovic, and he said that he should be more active in terms of doing something, that he shouldn't just go around in circles there, whatever. I mean, I cannot say this specifically now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did Mladic do something to Popovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He kicked him. He kicked him in the rear.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recall what Mladic said to Popovic regarding what he should be doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand that. I just heard him say that he should do something, that he shouldn't just be walking around. Do I have to say everything?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, the Court's heard everything. They've heard all kinds of things, so I don't think that's a problem. Tell us the whole story.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said, "Don't walk around there. Don't chase women's skirts. Do something."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were there any other superior officers that you noticed around at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Where was your commander, Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where Commander Blagojevic was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Popovic found Nikolic, then they went to the APCs that were behind the brigade headquarters. And soon after that, the crew came -- a crew from the Bratunac Brigade that had manned an APC of the Army of Republika Srpska -- or rather, they did not come on an APC. They just came there. It was just this crew that came.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: How many? How many crew members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There were about four or five of them there. They wanted to get the APC moving. They had a lot of trouble. They didn't succeed. I walked up. Momir spoke to me and I walked up to one of these APCs and I managed to get it going.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what kind of APCs that was that you got going. What kind of an APC was it, in terms of who did it belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an armoured personnel carrier of the UN, of the Dutch Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What colour was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: White with black UN lettering.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What did you do after you got that APC started up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got the APC started up, Nikolic came and sat in the APC with me. And Mile Petrovic did, too. Nikolic probably called him to come along with us, as well, and he said to me that we should drive in the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And so what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this other APC went behind us, the one that was driven by this crew.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What kind of APC was that, the other one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same one, the same one like the previous one, the one that I drove.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you drove this -- the one you started up and this crew drove another one. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were there any other vehicles with this -- with you and the other APC?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Are you asking me whether some other vehicle also went to Konjevic Polje or whether there were some other vehicles over there?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, just tell me what vehicles went to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure. I'm not sure, so I cannot say. I know that these two APCs went. I drove the first one. I don't know who drove the second one, one of the crew members. I'm trying to remember, and I tried to on Sunday as well when we talked. But I cannot say. I think -- I say I think, and it's hard to make any statements that I'm not sure of. I think that Colonel Popovic went in a Golf, in a navy blue Golf. Again I'm saying I'm not sure and I don't know because I confuse Zvornik -- I mean, when I went to Zvornik and when I went to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. What were Nikolic's orders to you on this -- for this trip to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing, just to go to Konjevic Polje. Once we got there, he ordered -- first he came out and he had a word with someone, someone. And then he said to follow the Golf driven by the civilian police. It was blue and white with a police light on the roof and a loudspeaker, a PA system, mounted on it. Once the Golf drove off perhaps 200 or 300 metres, he told us to follow it. You could hear some sound coming through the PA system from the police vehicle; however, the noise from the engines and the caterpillar on the asphalt was too loud, so you couldn't understand what was being said on the PA system.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Who was around to hear anything from a PA system?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who and where people were. I do know that there were soldiers lining the road. As for any other persons there, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What was the purpose of this trip where you were following a MUP vehicle with a loud speaker that's making some sort of announcement over the airway? What was the purpose of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the purpose was. My understanding was that this was just for the security of that vehicle, because the wood was the -- the trees in the woods were beginning to bloom, so it was difficult to see. There were people hiding in the woods who may have been shooting at the vehicles. That was my interpretation, and that was the only reason I could see for them to send the APC after that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you get an order to drive that APC down the road, that UN APC, to try to trick Muslims into surrendering to the UN?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you get such an order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was it possible that was the purpose of your trip?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. It calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would suggest this witness is somewhat on the adverse side of things, and I think a little help might be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think we already discussed this at the very beginning of the proceedings. I believe the question along these lines is allowed. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is it possible that this trip in the UN vehicle with the loudspeaker was to announce to the Muslims to surrender themselves to the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the purpose of that was. No one ever told me what those people were saying, what they would say, that they would say anything to begin with over the loudspeaker. I didn't know who was in this vehicle. This vehicle was just there. I didn't know who was inside it. It just drove off. Once it did, I was told to follow it. What the purpose of the whole thing was, I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Where did you first see this police vehicle and start following it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the vehicle was there at the junction when we came. It was there -- we didn't start out straight off. We spent some time there and then the other APC went towards Milici, Kasaba Milici, and we were there. Suddenly this vehicle drove off in the direction of Bratunac. Who was in it, I don't know. And once it was 200 or 300 metres from where we were, I was told to start up the APC and follow it without catching up, however, because the vehicle was moving quite slowly. So once we drove away from the junction, perhaps 200 or 300 metres away, up to 500 metres, I heard sounds coming from the loudspeaker. Something was being said, but there was too much background noise for me to understand what exactly was being said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you were at the intersection of Konjevic Polje at this time, did you see any Muslim prisoners anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not getting any interpretation. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Let's try again. When you were at the Konjevic Polje intersection at this time, did you see any Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a feature just across the way from the -- if you come from the general direction of Bratunac, you cross the street and there was a building there. There was some soldiers, soldiers I didn't recognise. There was some members of the MUP whom I didn't know either, and there was a building just before the junction to the right of the road where there were also people inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see a MUP officer named Nenad Djokic there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know who Nenad Djokic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nenad Djokic was -- I know a man named Nenad Djokic who was a member of the military police platoon but not a member of the MUP, Nenad Djokic. There was a Nenad Djokic with the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: How about Nenad Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember having seen him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know a Nenad Deronjic that was with MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see Nenad Deronjic in Konjevic Polje that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember seeing him there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: He was a member of the Bratunac MUP, wasn't he, at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was and he still is a member of the Bratunac MUP. I think he still is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you aware that he was identified by a Muslim survivor of an execution that occurred a short distance from Konjevic Polje that day as one of his executioners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Have you ever heard the allegation that some 16 Muslim prisoners were taken from Konjevic Polje intersection on a bus driven up a kilometre or two and shot by the banks of the Jadar River at about 11.00 a.m. on the morning of the 13th. Have you ever heard of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have never heard of that. The only thing I do know is that the vehicles that were -- the buses, the lorries, mostly buses, though, that were passing through Konjevic Polje while I was still at the junction there, they were passing through on their way to Konjevic Polje, or rather, on their way to Milici. They were transporting women and children, very few men, too, especially able-bodied men. There weren't too many on those buses. They were passing through without hindrance. No one stopped them. No one pulled up in Konjevic Polje. They were passing through and taking a left turn. Driving in front of them was always an UN jeep, a jeep belonging to the Dutch Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: While you were in Konjevic Polje, did you see three buses full of Muslim men followed by a green APC, and shortly after that followed by an excavator, not heading in the direction of Milici but heading in the direction of -- excuse me, heading in the direction of Milici towards Cerska. Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I did not see any APCs pass through, I'm sure about that. Although, I wasn't really paying attention, but I didn't see an excavator either, but I was paying attention to the buses and who was in them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Getting back to your -- now, you say you've left Konjevic Polje following a police vehicle with a megaphone, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went perhaps 2 or 3 kilometres further down the road toward Bratunac when the vehicle turned around in the middle of the road. As soon as it started turning, I stopped and I waited for it to finish turning around. So once this vehicle was done turning around, I drove to where I had enough space to turn around my own rather large vehicle which I was then driving for the first time. I turned around and drove back to Konjevic Polje, crossing the same distance as I had on the way to Bratunac. I returned to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you following that same police vehicle again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And its loudspeaker was continuing the whole time you were following it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know they were speaking on the way to Bratunac. Whether they were also speaking on the way back, I can't quite remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what happened when you got to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got to Konjevic Polje, I parked the APC where it had been. This other vehicle, I don't remember the other police vehicle being there. I wasn't sure where they had gone to, whether to Zvornik or Milici. I didn't know. Maybe it was parked behind some buildings somewhere I couldn't see it, but I know that when I came back I no longer saw it there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what happened in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two soldiers came along from the Dutch Battalion. Whether they got out of the vehicle or perhaps they, as far as I understood, came down from a checkpoint somewhere, if they had arrived on foot or wearing their equipment, I don't know, but they saw their own vehicle there. They came closer. I was all the time standing by the APC so that no one could steal any equipment from the vehicle. They said they wanted to be with us. They stayed with us for a while. A soldier came. I'm not sure from which unit. He wanted to trade a rifle with one of those soldiers, and the other soldier agreed immediately. When I saw what was happening, I told the soldier that it was absolutely out of the question for him to trade equipment with that other soldier. So we got into the APC and they wanted to go for a spin with us or whatever, and we headed back to Bratunac. We drove for about 2 or 3 kilometres, and again returned to Konjevic Polje. We started out towards Bratunac, but then we turned around and went back to Konjevic Polje. Back in Konjevic Polje, after a while, a convoy arrived of vehicles that were carrying women, children, from Srebrenica. The convoy was headed by a jeep, an all terrain vehicle, with two Dutch soldiers in it. They stopped right there. They were pulled up, and those two soldiers who were with us got into the jeep and drove off to Milisic [as interpreted] they never returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was Momir Nikolic with you when you were with these Dutch soldiers driving around in your APC -- in their APC?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Momir Nikolic was there when we followed the police vehicle. Whether he was there when the two Dutch soldiers were with us, I don't know. I can't remember. He drove to Bratunac in a vehicle, some vehicle, during that time. But I believe he went to Bratunac and then returned there. And we were there all the while. Whether he came with us when the two Dutch soldiers were there, I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you say "with us," who else was with you when you were driving around with the Dutch soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said when we set out from Bratunac he was there with me. I was driving the APC. Momir Nikolic was there and Mile Petrovic was there too.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was Mile Petrovic with you when you were driving with the Dutch soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did Mile Petrovic have a close family member that was killed by the Muslims during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In what action was his brother killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His brother was killed when an attack took place on Bjelovac from the enclave which at that time was an UN protected zone. The village of Bjelovac, the village in which he was born, his family was there. He lived there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: During your travels in this APC, did you get any Muslims -- any Muslims turn themselves in or did you capture them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't our assignment to capture anyone. I saw the detained Muslims, but as we were driving -- the Dutch soldiers may have been there. I'm not sure. I was driving, Momir Nikolic was there and Petrovic. On our way to Bratunac you couldn't hear a thing inside the APC. Momir Nikolic pulled me by the collar and he told me to pull over because two persons were noticed coming down towards the road. Two persons reached the road, the asphalt road, from a path through the forest. It was a wide path, a gravel track, and they reached the APC and someone opened the door. It was Mile or Nikolic and let them into the APC. We drove back to Konjevic Polje and we stopped there. Someone took those people away, some of the soldiers took them to the right where the other people were standing and there was a house there, a building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One last question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that Mile Petrovic was involved in killing any Muslim prisoners that day around Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-140 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think it's break time or end time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Given the last question, if the Prosecutor could pose it with a little more directness given the facts that he was aware of from his star witness Nikolic's testimony, because Nikolic said they captured six, they were in that APC and so on and so forth. So I would like to have that question posed directly to this witness at this point before we break for the day. Because the way it was posed, it is rather a general question and not very specific tailored to the facts, as we all know them to have been stated by Mr. Nikolic in this courtroom, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that is relevant at this moment, Mr. Karnavas. If you are going to ask this question, you have the full right at a stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I was merely trying to assist the Court, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we may find another opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have to stop here and the hearing will resume tomorrow at 9.00 in the same courtroom. And, Witness, I have to tell you that while you are in The Hague, you are still under the oath, so do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. You understand that? And please remain seated --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- when we leave this courtroom, and the usher will pull down the blinds and take you out of this courtroom, just out of the consideration of the caution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 1.47 p.m. to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of October, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
